title: I Enforced the Climbing-Gym Belay Card on the Setter Who Forgot His

parts.text: I sat the belay desk at 5:19 p.m. and the routesetter walked past with a rope and no card. The rule he wrote on the waiver wall said: BELAY CARD VISIBLE. NO EXCEPTIONS ON STAFF. I was twenty-nine, front desk, holding a new climber who had just failed her check. Setter Cole said, "I set the wall. I am the check." I pointed at his wall. He smirked. "Setters are the gym." I photographed the empty lanyard, the wall, and the time. Then I stopped his rope at the auto-belay gate and logged a safety hold. At 5:24 the manager asked why Cole's name was on a cardless-belay ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager can see Cole on the wall with no card against the rule he wrote.

social.video_title: The setter forgot the belay card he wrote — Part 1/2
social.description: New climber, a routesetter with no lanyard, and a wall rule. I held the rope. Would you have waved him through?

parts.text: Cole called it a joke until insurance asked for the hold log. I printed the ticket, the wall photo, and the empty lanyard. He retook the check with the new climber watching. Cole climbed with a bright card and told staff the rule was always about optics. Optics is a word setters use when a photo exists. Desk policy now has a second line: SETTERS ARE NOT THE CHECK. I keep spare cards in a labeled bin. Cole clips his. The wall finally matches the waiver.

social.video_title: Setters are not the belay check — Part 2/2
social.description: Insurance log, a retake, and a second line on the wall. Was setting ever a visible card?
